Detailed implementation plan: https://chatgpt.com/space/page_fa28a6b2fe70819199a0a178f96c7fb6
Current scope supersedes prior extraction/model research: CATEGORY LABELING ONLY. Data Labels catalog with names/descriptions, document/chunk targets and per-target automation; existing configured Decision model evaluates each category independently. Multiple labels or none may apply. Inclusion/exclusion assignments with optional per-resource text values (up to 200 characters); category/value chips; shared assignment editor, value suggestions, and selected-resource value management; inline chunk markers in PR 3. Values and their BO management were added by tasks zaq-kw0.30–zaq-kw0.36, superseding the original category-only restriction. No extraction, summarization, new text model or dedicated model selector. Automatic reset remains deferred to PR 2.
Manual document inclusions and exclusions survive re-ingestion. Old chunks and all assignments are deleted; new chunks receive automatic labels when eligible. Missing model skips automation without failing ingestion. Separate FK-backed tables prevent resource-ID collisions. Provisional server-owned probability cutoff 0.80 requires fixture calibration/review; persist decision policy and guard stale results.
Eighteen children preserve serial dependencies and cover persistence, Decision runtime, validated classification/edit Actions, generation lifecycle, scheduling, authorized projections, locators, UI, approval/E2E and review/coverage/final validation. PR 1 is implemented locally; gate .1 is resolved. Review/validation gate .19 remains open; UX approval .15 precedes E2E .16. Historical comments retain superseded research; this description and linked Page define current scope.

## Three PR delivery
# Three PR delivery plan

Deliver labeling in three independently reviewable PRs, merged in sequence. Storage and editing contracts support documents and chunks from PR 1; inline chunk visualization arrives in PR 3. Extraction and summarization remain future processors, with no implementation in these PRs.

| PR | Scope | Usable result and completion |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 1 Label management and manual labeling | Definitions/targets, typed assignments, authorization, Data → Labels, shared editor and document chips. Tasks 1, 2, 4, 8, 9, 12, 13; gate 19. | Users manually label documents. Chunk assignment/editor contracts exist. Automatic controls and reset stay disabled in UI and server until PR 2. |
| 2 Generic processing and automatic labeling | Existing Decision runtime, generation guards, generic dispatcher/worker and labeling processor, automatic document/chunk scheduling. Tasks 3, 5, 6, 21, 7; gate 20. | Every new chunk is evaluated when one or more chunk labels are automatic and the Decision model is configured. Missing configuration skips safely. |
| 3 Chunk visualization and editing | Source positions, safe Markdown markers, chunk names/chips, shared editor wiring and full integration. Tasks 10, 11, 14–18. | Users see/edit labels at chunk starting positions in the Ingested modal; completed-feature UX approval precedes consolidated E2E. |

Each PR includes migrations where needed, targeted tests and owning documentation. Apply review → coverage → final validation → human approval independently to each PR. Earlier PRs record pending feature E2E scenarios under task 16; they retain immediate unit/integration/LiveView checks and do not wait for downstream implementation. Preserve manual document inclusions/exclusions and cascade old chunk assignments from PR 1; PR 2 adds asynchronous generation safety.

Authoritative dependency order (stable task IDs): 1 -> 2 -> 4 -> 8 -> 9 -> 12 -> 13 -> 19 -> 3 -> 5 -> 6 -> 21 -> 7 -> 20 -> 10 -> 11 -> 14 -> 15 -> 16 -> 17 -> 18.
PR 1 gate zaq-kw0.19; PR 2 gate zaq-kw0.20; generic processing zaq-kw0.21. Existing automatic configuration means the Decision selector, not a new model selector. This delivery sequence supersedes the former numerical chain.

## PR 1 implementation status
Tasks 1/2/4/8/9/12/13 are implemented. 446 scoped regression tests pass including 12 properties; mix q passes; migration rollback/reapply passes on the dedicated test partition. Browser inspection confirms definition creation and manual document labels; existing Chromium/WebKit journeys: 141 pass, 2 pre-existing skips, 1 System Config navigation timeout. Firefox binary missing. Full precommit rerun is still exposing unchanged Python crawler/conversion fixtures/environment failures. Gate 19 remains in progress for validation/review/coverage; no Git commits or pushes. Automatic processing and inline chunk visualization remain PR 2/3.

## PR2 reviewed scope handoff (2026-11-04)
Dedicated epic zaq-kw0.42 now owns PR2 execution; its child contracts supersede earlier reset/resource-specific-classifier and automatic retry proposals. PR2 has 18 tasks, reusing IDs zaq-kw0.3/.5/.6/.21/.7/.20. PR1 gate zaq-kw0.19 remains open; PR3 starts after zaq-kw0.20.
No reset-to-automatic or classification suggestion workflow. Generic general.classify returns probabilities; shared RAG Decision threshold defaults to 80%, captured per reservation and changed only for future requests. Preflight failed interactive runs ask proceed without classification or cancel; unattended runs proceed without classification and report. Mid-run provider failures never block ingestion or trigger silent classification retries. Definition-change confirmation counts only current chunks carrying the changed label; accepted chunks are evaluated against all eligible automatic chunk labels, preserving manual overrides. No new-label backfill; full refresh requires deliberate reingestion. Not now retains stale labels in UI, authorized filters and usage counts. No token/cost estimate.
PR3 UX/E2E must cover those flows plus PR1 manual values/deletion and chunk visualization. Keep zaq-kw0.15 -> zaq-kw0.16 approval dependency; do not author new feature E2E before explicit completed-UX approval or close either gate for this planning work.

Candidate for Labeling model instead of general-purpose generation; requires provider-specific entities options, multiple-match policy and output normalization. Documentation research only; no inference benchmark and no Page/implementation changes.
